title: Fulfilling the Soul’s Deepest Needs | Sri Daya Mata

# Fulfilling the Soul’s Deepest Needs

### Self-Realization Fellowship
**A Spiritual Discourse Inspired by Sri Daya Mata**

---

### The Silent Hunger of the Heart

In the quiet moments of our lives, when the clamor of the external world momentarily fades, we are often confronted with a profound, aching emptiness. It is a subtle, persistent hunger that cannot be satisfied by any earthly possession, relationship, or sensory pleasure. Sri Daya Mata, one of the foremost disciples of Paramahansa Yogananda and the beloved third president of Self-Realization Fellowship, reminds us that this restlessness is not a curse, but a divine gift. It is the silent, sacred homesickness of the soul, yearning to return to its eternal source in God.

We spend our lives seeking fulfillment in the finite, expecting it to yield the Infinite. We seek perfect love in human relationships, perfect security in financial wealth, and perfect joy in fleeting experiences. Yet, every worldly gain eventually leaves us wanting more. The soul can never find lasting satisfaction in the material world because it is made in the image of the Divine. Its home is in the boundless, ever-existing, ever-conscious, ever-new Bliss of Spirit. Until we realize this truth, we will continue to wander through the halls of life, hungry and unfulfilled.

Our beloved Guru, Paramahansa Yogananda, taught us that the greatest adventure in human life is the journey back to God. He showed us that the Divine is not a distant, uncaring ruler, but our very own nearest of the near, dearest of the dear. Sri Daya Mata beautifully reflects this devotion, urging us to approach the Divine Mother with the simple, trusting heart of a child.

> "Do not seek God only when the world wounds you. Seek Him because you cannot live without Him. He is the life of your life, the sight of your eyes, the love of your heart. In Her presence alone is the absolute fulfillment of all your desires."

---

### Awakening the Divine Will Within Us

To bridge the gap between our current state of restlessness and the absolute fulfillment of the soul, we must awaken and direct our inner faculties. Among these, the most powerful is our will power. Sri Daya Mata frequently spoke of the importance of active, dynamic will in the spiritual life. Gurudeva taught that will power is the instrument by which the Divine Mother works through us. When we align our human will with the Divine Will, we become channels of miraculous transformation.

Many seekers live passively, waiting for God to drop realization into their laps. But spiritual progress requires dynamic effort. We must make the conscious choice to seek Him, to sit in meditation even when the mind is restless, and to hold onto His peace amidst the trials of daily life. By applying our will toward spiritual goals, we transform our dry intellectual theories into living, breathing spiritual realizations.

To cultivate this divine will, we must free ourselves from the enslavement of bad habits and mechanical living. Every time we choose to meditate instead of indulging in idle distraction, we strengthen our spiritual will. Every time we answer anger with love, we assert the supremacy of the soul over the lower ego. In this way, our lives become a continuous offering, a dynamic prayer of attunement with the Infinite.

---

### Cultivating the Inner Sanctuary of Silence

We cannot hear the whisper of the Divine Mother if our minds are constantly flooded with the noise of the world. It is essential to carve out a sacred space within our daily routine for silent communion. Sri Daya Mata emphasized that meditation is not merely a practice of concentration, but a deep, loving conversation with the Beloved.

When we sit in the silence, we must lay down all our worries, our responsibilities, and our anxieties at the feet of the Lord. For those moments, the world does not exist; only you and God exist. It is in this profound stillness that the soul’s deepest needs are met. The Divine Mother does not demand complex rituals or theological knowledge. She demands our love, our sincerity, and our undivided attention.

> "If you only knew how much She loves you, how She longs to fold you in Her arms of light and wash away all your sorrows! But She waits for you to turn your face toward Her. In the temple of silence, She is waiting."

In deep meditation, as the breath becomes calm and the thoughts subside, the soul begins to taste the nectar of divine love. This love is unlike any earthly affection; it is completely unconditional, unchangeable, and limitlessly expanding. When we touch this inner spring of grace, the thirst of the soul is instantly quenched, and we realize that we have always been held in the tender embrace of God.

---

### Practical Spiritual Habits for Daily Life

To maintain this state of inner fulfillment amidst the duties of daily life, Sri Daya Mata recommended several practical, life-transforming habits:

* **Begin and End the Day with God:** Dedicate your first thoughts upon waking, and your last thoughts before falling asleep, to the Divine Mother. Offer yourself entirely to Her keeping.
* **Practice the Presence of God:** Throughout the day, carry on a silent, mental conversation with the Lord. Whether you are working, eating, or walking, whisper in your heart: *"I love Thee, Lord. Guide my thoughts, my words, and my actions."*
* **Meditate Daily with Devotion:** Establish a regular, uninterrupted time for deep meditation. Use the sacred techniques taught by the Gurus of Self-Realization Fellowship to quiet the body and mind, and then sit in the subsequent stillness, absorbing the peace of the soul.
* **Perform Selfless Service:** Serve others not for recognition, but as an offering to the Divine who dwells within them. Selfless service purifies the heart and expands our consciousness.
* **Surrender Your Worries:** When anxieties arise, consciously hand them over to the Divine Mother. Say to Her: *"Lord, this is Thy problem. I will do my best, but the results are Thine."*

---

### The Sweetness of Unconditional Surrender

Ultimately, the soul’s deepest needs are fulfilled through the sweet grace of surrender. We must let go of the illusion that we are in sole control of our destiny. When we surrender our egoic pride, our fears, and our attachments to the Divine Mother, we experience a freedom that passes all understanding. We realize that the same power that guides the stars and maintains the cosmos is tenderly guiding every detail of our lives.

Sri Daya Mata’s life was a radiant testament to this surrender. Her every word, her gentle smile, and her deep compassion flowed from her complete reliance on God and Guru. She showed us that by empty-ing ourselves of the small "I," we allow ourselves to be filled with the infinite ocean of His light, joy, and wisdom.

Let us make the determination to seek this divine communion above all else. Let us not delay our search for tomorrow, for tomorrow is a thief that steals our precious present. Today, in this very moment, let us open the doors of our hearts and welcome the Divine Mother into our lives.

---

### A Closing Prayer and Blessing

*O Divine Mother, beloved Father, dearest Friend, and Guru,*  
*We offer the devotion of our hearts at Thy lotus feet. We surrender all our worries, our struggles, and our dreams into Thy loving hands. Forgive us for the times we have forgotten Thee in our search for worldly happiness. Fill our souls with Thy pure, unconditional love, and grant us the strength to always keep our minds stayed on Thee. Let Thy peace shine through our eyes, and let Thy love flow through our actions to comfort all who cross our path.*  

*May we ever remain anchored in Thy joy, resting securely in the temple of Thy silence.*  

*Jai Guru. Jai Ma.*
